newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK COURT ORDERS MUTUAL FUND, BROKERS TO PAY 360MLN DRS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK COURT ORDERS MUTUAL FUND, BROKERS TO PAY 360MLN DRS.

text.p: A Greek court has ordered General Bank's mutual fund management company, Avax Securities and Petropoulakis Securities to pay an investor a total of 360 million drachmas in connection with share transactions, court officals told Reuters.
The court of first instances said its decision was based on legal stock exchange transactions ordered by investor Panayiotis Tryfonas.
Tryfonas had asked the court to order General Bank's mutual fund management company and two Athens bourse member brokers to make the payment in connection with share transactions on his behalf.
But the general manager of the mutual fund management company and the vice-president of Petropoulakis Securities vowed to appeal the decision.

"There is a court order to freeze the assets of Tryfonas issued on November 27 that this court might not have been aware of," said Andreas Papaspyrou, general manager at General AEDAK. "We are going to appeal the decision."
General AEDAK had refused to redeem Tryfonas' mutual fund shares in November, he said.
"We are aware of the court decision," said Anastasios Petropoulakis, vice-president at Petropoulakis Securities. "We are confident that we will win the case in court."
Petropoulakis said his brokerage had refused to pay Tryfonas cash for the sale of his shares in Magrizos November.
Magrizos shares were at the centre of the Delta Securities scandal that shook the bourse in early November 1996.
Tryfonas has also asked the court to force Komninos Securities and Commercial Securities to pay him 100 million drachmas but no decision has been issued yet.
The court also ordered the seizure of Delta Securities' assets for the sum of 14.8 million drachmas on behalf of Polyxeni Pandazidou, court officials said.
Pantazidou had allegedly given the president of Delta Securities 47 million drachmas in June 1996 to buy her government securities but she never took physical possesion of the debt paper.
The court rejected Pandazidou's suit against the Athens stock exchange depository for the same case, the officials said.
Auditors looking into the Delta Securities scandal submitted their findings to the court on Tuesday, the officials said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
